title: Machine learning identifies new CYP2C9-inhibiting drugs and drug metabolites
summary: A structure-, dynamics- and physicochemical-feature machine-learning approach predicted CYP2C9 inhibition and experimentally identified four drugs—vatalanib, piriqualone, ticagrelor and cloperidone—as strong inhibitors, plus sertindole, asapiprant, duvelisib and dasatinib as moderate inhibitors in reported assays. Vatalanib had a reported CYP2C9 inhibition IC50 of 0.067 μM. Separate metabolism assays characterized CYP2C9-produced metabolites for abemaciclib, cloperidone, vatalanib and tarafenacin.
ai_technology: Machine-learning inhibitor predictors combining CYP2C9 structural/dynamics information with inhibitor physicochemical properties
organization: INSERM; CNRS and Université de Paris; Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers; Université de Lorraine; Nantes Université

evidence.tested: A structure-, dynamics- and physicochemical-feature machine-learning approach predicted CYP2C9 inhibition and experimentally identified four drugs—vatalanib, piriqualone, ticagrelor and cloperidone—as strong inhibitors, plus sertindole, asapiprant, duvelisib and dasatinib as moderate inhibitors in reported assays.
evidence.unknown: Inhibition and metabolite findings are from the reported in vitro systems and do not by themselves establish clinically relevant drug–drug interactions, exposure changes, or patient harm. Reported inhibition strengths are assay-specific; clinical relevance depends on dose, exposure and context and requires pharmacokinetic/clinical assessment.
evidence.ai_role: The authors used machine-learning models to prioritize drug-like compounds for CYP2C9 inhibition testing. Follow-up in vitro assays identified the listed strong and moderate inhibitors; CYP2C9 metabolism assays separately characterized metabolites of four drugs.
